notes: First Waymo market. Early Rider Program launched April 2017 (invite-only, safety driver). Waymo One commercial service launched 2018-12-05 (limited, safety driver retained for most rides). Fully driverless rides opened to the general public 2020-10-08, PR release https://waymo.com/blog/2020/10/waymo-is-opening-its-fully-driverless-service-in-phoenix/ ; service area ~50 sq mi at 2020 launch, later expanded to ~315 sq mi (2025 figures per thedriverlessdigest.com). Phoenix Sky Harbor airport curbside service: Trusted Tester rides began Nov 2022, rider-only/24-7 curbside by Dec 2023-2024 (first airport in the world with driverless AV curbside service) https://www.skyharbor.com/about-phx/news-media/press-releases/phoenix-sky-harbor-becomes-first-airport-in-the-world-to-offer-waymo-rider-only-autonomous-vehicle-service/ . Freeway driving added in Phoenix per 2025 year-in-review.

Silicon Valley/Peninsula (Mountain View, Los Altos, Palo Alto, parts of Sunnyvale, ~27 sq mi) added 2025-03-11 (https://www.cnbc.com/2025/03/11/waymo-expands-its-robotaxi-service-in-the-san-francisco-bay-area.html); South Bay peninsula cities (Brisbane, South SF, San Bruno, Millbrae, Burlingame) added later 2025. CPUC regulatory filing (Aug 2025) showed 1,429 vehicles registered for CA operations, 875 based at SF depots (per thelastdriverlicenseholder.com citing CPUC). SFO airport service approved/launched 2026-01-29 (https://waymo.com/blog/2026/01/waymo-rides-at-sfo/); San Jose Mineta airport and freeway access added per Nov 2025 CPUC approval (https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/22/waymo-gets-regulatory-approval-to-expand-across-bay-area-and-southern-california/). Total Bay Area service area ~260 sq mi as of late 2025.
